title: EATS: Scaling Tool-Use Experience for Medical Reasoning Agents
abstract: arXiv:2611.33897v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Medical reasoning agents combine large language model (LLM) reasoning with clinical workflows and specialized neural tools. However, general-purpose LLMs receive limited training exposure to domain-specific medical tools, and the uncertainty and distributional shifts of neural tool outputs make selecting tools from simple descriptions significantly more challenging than in deterministic settings such as calculators or dictionary lookups. In this paper, we propose EATS, an experience-augmented tool selection strategy that leverages accumulated tool-use trajectories to improve tool selection in medical reasoning agents. EATS constructs a memory of past interactions, including queries, tool choices, arguments, and self-evaluated feedback, and retrieves relevant experiences to guide tool selection for new queries. As memory construction does not require ground-truth supervision, EATS scales naturally with test-time experience. We evaluate EA

translated_title: EATS：为医学推理智能体扩展工具使用经验
translated_abstract: 医学推理智能体将大语言模型（LLM）的推理能力与临床工作流程及专用神经工具相结合。然而，通用LLM在领域特定医学工具方面的训练接触有限，且神经工具输出的不确定性和分布偏移使得仅凭简单描述来选择工具，比在计算器或词典查询等确定性场景中更具挑战性。本文提出了EATS，一种经验增强的工具选择策略，它利用累积的工具使用轨迹来改进医学推理智能体中的工具选择。EATS构建了一个过往交互的记忆库，内容包括查询、工具选择、参数以及自我评估的反馈，并检索相关经验来指导新查询的工具选择。由于记忆构建不需要真值监督，EATS能够随测试时经验的积累自然地扩展。
tldr: EATS提出了一种无需真值监督的经验增强工具选择策略，通过构建并检索累积的工具使用轨迹记忆（包括查询、工具选择、参数和自我评估反馈），随测试时经验的增长自然扩展，从而显著提升医学推理智能体的工具选择能力。
en_tdlr: EATS is an experience-augmented tool selection strategy that builds and retrieves a memory of accumulated tool-use trajectories—requiring no ground-truth supervision and scaling naturally with test-time experience—to improve tool selection for medical reasoning agents.
